name: History and period worlds
purpose: how work used to be: the origins of safety law, pay and record keeping, fair trading and consumer protection, office work before computers, change over time

identity.place: One cotton-weaving town in a temperate valley, seen at two dates in the life of its main firm. The 1890s: the firm's north-light weaving shed of about 800 looms, its counting house in the stone office block beside the shed, and the town's market street on a market day. The 1950s: the same firm's general office, in the same stone block, sixty years on. Two dates are kept on purpose and no others: the 1890s carry the origins of factory safety law, wages and records, and fair trading; the 1950s carry how office work used to be done. Every scene says which date it is.
architecture: the town is built of local buff-grey sandstone, blackened by coal smoke, with blue-grey slate roofs; terraced streets climb the valley side; the firm's tall square chimney stands over the shed

the weaving shed: one storey under a sawtooth north-light roof (glazed slopes facing north, slated slopes facing south, about 30 degrees), on a grid of slim hollow cast-iron columns carrying cast-iron gutter beams at about 3.5 m, the ridges at about 4.6 m; stone-flag floors; lime-washed stone walls; line shafts on brackets along the column rows driving cross-shafts and leather belts down to every loom

the office block beside the shed: two storeys of dressed sandstone, tall timber sash windows with small panes, plastered walls, timber floors, panelled timber doors and partitions with glazed upper panels, a cast-iron fireplace in the principal rooms

the market street: three-storey stone buildings with shops below, timber shop fronts with small-paned windows and painted fascia boards (slots), a wide street of stone setts with stone flag pavements and kerbs, gas street lamps on cast-iron columns, a stone drinking trough
1890s lighting is gas: wall brackets and pendants with glass globes; 1950s lighting is electric: opal glass pendant globes and a few fluorescent tubes
identity.materials: buff-grey sandstone (blackened outside, clean inside), blue-grey slate, lime-wash, cast iron painted dark green or black, oak and pitch pine joinery, brass fittings, leather (belts, ledger bindings, stool seats), cotton cloth in grey and cream, canvas awnings; in the 1950s also brown linoleum, green-grey painted steel, cream paint and Bakelite. The firm's colour is a deep bottle green (the shed's cast iron, the office doors, later the filing cabinets), with signal red only where it is red in life (a fire bucket, a pillar box on the street)
inhabited: 1890s work in progress: cloth growing on the looms, full and empty pirns in skips, weft baskets, a weaver's shawl on a peg, ledgers open on the desks, wage packets laid out in rows (slots), produce heaped on the stalls
1950s work in progress: sheets wound into typewriters with carbon paper between them, files in wire trays, a teacup and saucer, an ashtray with a stubbed cigarette, a cardigan over a chair back
the firm's systems: notices pinned at the shed door (slots), a time clock or a pay window, a fire bucket on a hook, a speaking tube in the 1890s office, a switchboard-fed telephone in the 1950s one
wear and age: worn flags in the alleys, cotton fluff on every ledge in the shed, ink stains on desks, scuffed linoleum, a cracked pane
scale: a person is about 1.7 m tall in the 1890s and about 1.75 m in the 1950s; children of 11 to 13 worked half time in the 1890s shed (C7 brief, age-accurate)

the shed's bays about 3.6 m by 6 m between columns; 3.5 m to the gutter beams and 4.6 m to the ridges; looms about 2.1 m long, 1.0 m deep and 1.2 m high, set back to back in pairs with alleys about 0.8 m wide between their fronts; four looms to a weaver
the office block's rooms about 3.6 m high with sash windows from a sill at 0.9 m to a head at about 2.9 m; doors about 2.1 by 0.9 m
a clerk's high sloping desk about 1.1 m high at its front edge, its stool about 0.8 m; a ledger up to 0.5 by 0.4 m and 0.2 m thick
1950s desks about 0.75 m high, typewriter tables about 0.66 m, four-drawer filing cabinets about 1.32 m tall
the market street about 12 m between building fronts with 2 m pavements; a stall about 2.4 m long with its board at about 0.9 m
identity.default_light: Daylight on an ordinary working day in autumn: in the 1890s scenes a grey, smoky, slightly golden light, soft and diffuse; in the 1950s scene a cleaner bright overcast daylight. Gas or electric lights are lit only where the scene says so.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one town (each scene names the ones its camera can see): buff-grey sandstone, cast iron painted deep bottle green, worn stone flags or setts, small-paned timber windows, a ledger or paper record, the firm's tall square chimney or the sawtooth roof seen through a window, cotton (cloth, bales, pirns).
avoid: anachronisms: nothing from after the scene's date (no electric light, plastics or typewriters in the 1890s scenes; no computers, photocopiers, plastic furniture or ballpoint-pen clutter in the 1950s office)
a costume-drama gloss: the period is ordinary working life, worn and used, not a museum
real firms, real towns, readable words or numbers on signs, ledgers, posters or papers (they are slots)
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
mixing the two dates in one picture
a moving belt, a lamp, a column or a window behind a character's head
identity.outside: Beyond the town: the valley sides of rough pasture with dry-stone walls, more mill chimneys down the valley with a soft haze of smoke, a pale sky.

scenes.what: the firm's north-light weaving shed in the 1890s, seen down an alley between two rows of power looms: looms on both sides, leather belts dropping from the overhead shafts, slim cast-iron columns, the sawtooth glazing above and the lime-washed stone end wall at the far end
scenes.for: how work used to be: the origins of factory safety law, unguarded machinery, child half-timers, noise and dust, long hours, the factory inspector
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs across the looms (the alley's centre line is at x 0); y runs along the alley away from the camera to the shed's end wall (y 15.0); z up from the stone-flag floor. The date is the 1890s.

Structure: slim hollow cast-iron columns on a grid at x -2.2 and 2.2 (in the lines between loom pairs) and y 7.2, 10.8 and 14.4; cast-iron gutter beams at 3.5 m; the sawtooth north-light roof above with its glazed slopes facing the camera's left, ridges at 4.6 m.

Looms: two rows face each other across the alley, each a run of Lancashire looms 2.1 m long set end to end: the right row's fronts (the cloth and breast beam side) along x 0.4, the left row's along x -0.4, from y 4.6 to 13.3; their backs (the warp beams) toward the columns, where the next rows stand back to back with them. The alley between the fronts is 0.8 m wide. Each loom has its driving pulley at its far end (as seen from the camera) with a belt rising to a cross-shaft at 3.0 m; line shafts run along the column lines at x -1.4 and 1.4.

Beyond the looms (y 13.3 to 15.0): a cross gangway along the end wall. The end wall (y 15.0): lime-washed sandstone, a panelled door at x -2.8 to -1.6 (2.4 m) with a gas lamp bracket above it, nothing else.

Cast spots: a weaver standing in the alley at the third loom on the right, facing it in profile (feet x 0.1, y 9.2; head top about 1.62 m); an overlooker or a factory inspector standing in the cross gangway at the alley's far end, facing the camera (feet x -0.4, y 14.1).

Camera: x -0.3, y 1.2 (in the cross gangway at the near end of the alley), standing eye height 1.6 m, turned 6 degrees right of the y axis; lens like 35 mm (55 degrees across); no tilt; the horizon at 46 percent of the frame height.
scenes.camera: Standing eye height 1.6 m at the near end of the alley, looking straight down it and turned 6 degrees right, so the view is not symmetrical; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt, verticals stay vertical. One strong vanishing point: horizon at y 497 (46 percent); the alley, the loom fronts, the shafts and the belts' rows meet at x about 766 on the horizon; lines across the shed (the end wall's base, the gutter beams) run very nearly level.
scenes.composition: The alley leads the eye from the bottom centre to the end wall, a calm lime-washed band across the middle (its visible part from x 394 to 1201, the floor line at about y 707 to 716, the gutter beam line at about y 236 to 248), with the panelled door at its left (x 422 to 589, top y 388). The two rows of looms close in from both sides: the right row's front edge from x 1142, y 710 near the camera back to x 873, y 558 at the far end; the left row's from x 711, y 716 to x 751, y 558. Belts rise from the looms to the shafts: on the right at x 1101 (y 164 to 639), x 1029 (y 236 to 609) and x 983 (from y 281); on the left at x 569, 613 (y 230 to 611) and 640. Columns stand in the lines beyond the looms: x 155 (base y 1008) and x 1510 (base y 971) near the camera, rising out of the top, then x 389 and 1239 further in. The sawtooth roof's glazing fills the top of the frame (a far rooflight about x 813, y 58). Free zones for the cast, nothing in front of head or chest: (1) the weaver at the third right-hand loom, seen full length in profile (head top x 859, y 492; feet x 859, y 866), the head against the lime-washed end wall (behind point x 0.39 on the wall, 1.43 to 1.63 m high), about 125 px left of the nearest belt (x 983) and 250 px right of the left-hand belts; (2) the overlooker at the far end, facing the camera (head top x 752, y 475; feet x 752, y 727), the head against the end wall (behind point x -0.41, 1.62 to 1.76 m high), about 110 px right of the left-hand belt and 160 px right of the door. What shows the height: the columns run out of the top of the frame and the sawtooth roof and its glazing fill the top band.
scenes.light: Main set: a grey autumn morning in the 1890s. Daylight comes only from the north-light glazing overhead, from the upper left: soft, even and cool, falling on the tops of the looms, the warp threads and the cloth, with soft shadows to the right and below every loom and belt. A faint haze of cotton fluff and humidity hangs in the air and softens the far end (haze up to 0.2 at the end wall, 14 m away). The gas lamp over the door is unlit. The belts and the picking sticks catch a dull sheen.
scenes.far: The whole shed: the end wall with its door and gas bracket, the roof and its glazing, the gutter beams, the columns, the shafts and belts, the stone-flag floor, and all the looms beyond the first pair (the weaver stands in front of the third right-hand loom, which is far).
scenes.mid: Nothing: the alley is open between the camera and both members of the cast.
scenes.near: The first loom on each side, cropped by the bottom corners (their breast beams and cloth beams about y 710 to 716 at their near ends, running out of the bottom), framing the alley.

scenes.what: the firm's counting house in the 1890s, on the ground floor of the stone office block: a long high double desk for the clerks in the middle of the room, the safe and the copying press against the far wall, and the small pay hatch in the far wall through which wages are paid
scenes.for: how records and money used to be kept: wages day, ledgers and double entry, checking the books, a clerk's fraud, the first rules on pay
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs from the window wall (x 0, left) to the right-hand wall (x 6.0, with the fireplace near the camera); y runs from the near wall (behind the camera) to the far wall (y 8.5); z up. The ceiling is at 3.6 m. The date is the 1890s.

Far wall (y 8.5): plaster painted a pale stone colour above a pitch-pine dado of vertical boards to 1.2 m. From left to right: a green-painted iron safe in the far left corner (x 0.15 to 0.95, 1.2 m tall); a framed notice of rules (a slot) at x 3.0 to 3.5, 1.8 to 2.2 m; a round wall clock with a plain face (no numerals) at x 3.9, 2.6 m; the cast-iron copying press on a small stand at x 3.4, y 8.15 (top 1.25 m); the pay hatch, a small sliding glazed hatch to the wages passage beyond, from x 4.6 to 5.2 and 0.9 to 1.3 m, with a shelf in front and a tray of wage tins beside it. The right-hand wall meets the far wall at x 6.0.
Window wall (x 0): two tall small-paned sash windows from y 1.2 to 2.4 and 3.4 to 4.6 (sills 0.9 m, heads 2.9 m), both beside and behind the camera's left; plain plaster from y 4.6 to the far corner.

The clerks' desk: a long high double desk of pitch pine from x 1.0 to 4.0, y 5.0 to 5.8, its two sloping lids meeting at a flat ridge with inkwells, the near lid's front edge at 1.1 m and the far one's at 1.15 m, on square legs with a foot rail; tall stools behind both sides, one pushed back. Ledgers open on the lids. A gas pendant with a glass globe hangs over the desk to 2.4 m.

Cast spots: a clerk standing at the far side of the desk facing the camera, writing in a ledger (feet x 2.3, y 6.25; head top 1.68 m); the manager standing at the near side of the desk's left end, turned to the ledger, seen from behind in three-quarter (feet x 1.5, y 4.35); the cashier standing at the pay hatch with their back to the camera (feet x 4.9, y 8.0).

Camera: x 4.4, y 0.4 (near the fireplace), standing eye height 1.6 m, turned 14 degrees left of the y axis (toward the windows); lens like 35 mm (55 degrees across); no tilt; the horizon at 46 percent of the frame height.

scenes.light: Main set: a grey autumn afternoon in the 1890s. scenes.what: the town's market street on a market day in the 1890s: a grocer's stall with a canvas awning and brass scales standing on the pavement in front of the plain sandstone side wall of the market hall, its tall arched openings either side, stone setts in the road and a gas lamp at the kerb
scenes.for: how trade used to be: weights and measures, food that was not what it claimed, serving a customer, the market inspector, public health in the street
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the street from left to right; y runs across it away from the camera; z up from the road. The date is the 1890s, a market day.

The market hall's side wall (y 8.0): dressed buff-grey sandstone, blackened in streaks, a plain plinth to 0.6 m; tall round-arched openings 2 m wide closed by dark iron gates, one from x -3.0 to -1.0 (springing at 2.4 m, crown 3.4 m) and the next from x 5.0 to 7.0; between them a plain stretch of wall 6 m long. The wall rises out of the top of the frame.
The hall's pavement of stone flags from y 6.0 (the kerb, about 0.12 m high) to the wall.

The grocer's stall on the pavement: a trestle board from x 1.0 to 3.4, y 6.4 to 7.3, at 0.9 m; a canvas awning on four wooden poles, its front edge at 2.3 m (y 6.2), sloping back to 2.0 m (y 7.6); on the board baskets of apples and potatoes, sacks with turned-down tops, butter on a slab, eggs in a basket, and a brass balance scale with a set of weights at x 2.0, y 6.8. Another stall's awning shows at the left edge (its right end about x -1.6).
A gas street lamp on a cast-iron column at the kerb at x 4.5, y 5.9 (lantern at about 3.2 m).

scenes.what: the firm's general office in the 1950s, in the same stone office block: rows of typing desks with manual typewriters, typists' chairs, a run of green steel filing cabinets against the cream inner wall, a wall clock and a calendar, opal glass pendant lights
scenes.for: how office work used to be done: typing and carbon copies, paper files and their security, a supervisor's rules, smoking at desks, unequal pay, work before computers
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs along the room from its front wall (x 0, left) to its back (x 12, right); y runs from the window wall (y 0, behind the camera) to the inner wall (y 7.0); z up. The ceiling is at 3.6 m. The date is the 1950s.

A panelled door painted deep bottle green at its left end (x 1.0 to 1.9, 2.1 m). A plain round electric wall clock at x 4.2, 2.6 m. A run of four green-grey steel four-drawer filing cabinets standing against the wall from x 6.3 to 7.7 (1.32 m tall, 0.4 m deep), a wall calendar above them (x 6.6 to 7.1, 1.6 to 2.1 m). scenes.light: Main set: a bright overcast morning in the 1950s. Daylight from the tall windows behind the camera lights the room from the front: faces, typewriters and paper evenly lit, soft shadows falling away from the camera onto the desks' far sides and the floor, the inner wall evenly bright. The opal pendants are on, a soft extra glow from above. A thin haze of cigarette smoke under the ceiling (haze about 0.1).
scenes.far: The room's shell: the inner wall with its door, clock, calendar, picture rail and skirting; the filing cabinets; the floor of brown linoleum; the pendants; and the typists' chairs at row B, drawn empty (the typists sit in them, in front of the far layer).
scenes.mid: Row B's desks and everything on them: the typewriters, trays, paper, carbon sheets and ashtrays (each desk stands in front of its typist's knees).
scenes.near: Row A's desks and chairs, cropped by the bottom edge (a typewriter's carriage and a chair back showing), framing the lower edge.

cast.role: 1890s working people of the town (C13): weavers (women and men) in shawls, aprons and clogs, child half-timers aged 11 to 13 (C7 brief, age-accurate), a tackler, an overlooker, a factory inspector, clerks, a cashier and a manager in dark suits, stallholders and customers, a market inspector
1950s office staff (C13): typists, an office supervisor, clerks and a manager in the dress of the time

objects.power loom: a Lancashire power loom about 2.1 m long, 1.0 m deep and 1.2 m high: a cast-iron side frame at each end, the warp beam at the back, the healds and the reed in the sley across the middle, the shuttle box at each end of the sley with a wooden picking stick, the cloth beam at the front with the woven cloth, a breast beam the weaver leans over, a weft fork; the driving pulley and its leather belt at one end; painted dark green, worn bright where hands touch
objects.line shaft and belts: overhead power: a long iron shaft about 75 mm across turning in bearings on brackets bolted to the columns, with pulleys along it; flat leather belts about 50 mm wide running down from the pulleys to each loom's driving pulley, slightly sagging
objects.cast-iron column: a slim hollow cast-iron column about 0.15 m across with a moulded base and a bracket cap carrying the gutter beams and a shaft bearing bracket, painted dark bottle green
objects.north-light roof: a sawtooth roof: rows of steep glazed slopes facing one way (small panes in timber glazing bars, a little sooty) and slated slopes facing the other, on timber rafters, the cast-iron gutter beams running under the valleys
objects.weft skip: a wicker skip about 0.6 by 0.4 m and 0.35 m deep, holding wooden pirns wound with weft
objects.gas lamp: an 1890s gas light: a brass wall bracket or pendant pipe with a small tap, a glass globe or a cup-shaped shade around the flame
objects.fire bucket: a round red-painted iron bucket with a rounded bottom, hung on a hook on a column or a wall
objects.high clerk's desk: a high sloping clerk's desk in pine or mahogany about 1.1 m high at its front: a hinged sloping lid with a ledge along the bottom edge, a flat strip at the top with an inkwell and a pen groove, on four square legs with a footrail; several desks often joined in a long run
objects.clerk's stool: a tall wooden stool about 0.8 m high with a round seat, four splayed legs and a ring footrest
objects.ledger: a large account ledger up to 0.5 by 0.4 m and 0.2 m thick, bound in leather with a reinforced spine and corners; pages ruled in columns (abstract lines, no numbers)
objects.copying press: a cast-iron letter copying press about 0.4 m tall: a flat bed, a heavy plate screwed down by a central screw turned with a two-armed handle ending in brass balls
objects.office safe: a green-painted iron safe about 1.2 m tall with a brass keyhole cover and a turning handle on its door
objects.pay window: a small sliding glazed hatch in a timber partition with a shelf below it, through which wages are paid
objects.market stall: a market stall: a trestle board about 2.4 by 0.9 m at about 0.9 m high, a canvas awning on wooden poles, baskets, sacks and crates of produce, a set of brass balance scales with weights
objects.horse and cart: a two-wheeled tradesman's cart with high spoked wheels and shafts, a horse in harness standing in the shafts, a nosebag
objects.gas street lamp: a cast-iron lamp column about 3.5 m tall with a fluted base, a ladder bar, and a square glazed lantern on top
objects.typewriter: a 1950s manual typewriter about 0.45 m wide: a heavy black or grey-green body, four rows of round keys (no letters shown), a carriage with a roller and a return lever on the left, a ribbon spool on each side, paper wound in with carbon sheets between
objects.filing cabinet: a four-drawer steel filing cabinet about 1.32 m tall, painted green-grey, each drawer with a label holder (a slot) and a pull handle
objects.Bakelite telephone: a black Bakelite desk telephone with a round dial (no numbers shown) and a handset on a cradle, a coiled cord
objects.typist's chair: a 1950s typist's chair: a small padded seat and a small padded backrest on a curved steel stem, on a four-legged base
objects.opal pendant: an electric light: an opal white glass globe on a metal rod or chain from a ceiling rose
objects.handcart: a two-wheeled wooden handcart: a shallow flat bed about 1.5 by 0.9 m with low sides, two large spoked wheels on an iron axle, two long handles, a prop leg at the front
objects.typing desk: a 1950s typing desk about 1.1 by 0.7 m with its top at about 0.66 m (lower than a writing desk): an oak top, a pedestal of three drawers on one side, a sliding shelf, a wire paper tray on the top
